# isException

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is an `Exception`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isException() — Checks whether a value is an `Exception`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isException(value: unknown): value is Exception;
```

The library's own hierarchy only. A plain `Error` does not qualify, which is exactly what makes the check useful in a `catch` block that has to tell the two apart.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is an `Exception`; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `Exception` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isException(new IllegalArgumentException()); // => true
isException(new Error()); // => false
isException({}); // => false
isException(null); // => false
```
